events.title: Hannibal ambushes a Roman army at Lake Trasimene
events.description: In morning mist on the lake shore, Hannibal trapped the consul Flaminius's army, killing about 15,000 Romans. The disaster led Rome to appoint Fabius Maximus as dictator.
events.html: In morning mist on the lake shore, Hannibal trapped the consul Flaminius's army, killing about 15,000 Romans. The disaster led Rome to appoint Fabius Maximus as dictator.

events.title: William Clito defeats Thierry of Alsace at Axspoele
events.description: William Clito, imposed as Count of Flanders by Louis VI of France after the murder of Charles the Good, defeated his rival Thierry of Alsace at Axspoele. Clito died at the siege of Aalst that year, and Thierry became count.

events.title: Külüg Khan is enthroned as emperor of the Yuan Dynasty
events.description: Khayishan was enthroned as Külüg Khan, Emperor Wuzong of the Yuan Dynasty of China. He is regarded as the seventh Great Khan of the Mongol Empire, though the title was only nominal because the empire had divided.

events.title: An Imperial–Spanish army destroys the French at Landriano
events.description: Antonio de Leyva's Imperial–Spanish army destroyed the French army of the Count of Saint-Pol at Landriano in the War of the League of Cognac. It temporarily ended the struggle between Francis I and Emperor Charles V for control of northern Italy.

events.title: Edward Cornwallis founds Halifax, Nova Scotia
events.description: British settlers arrived to build a fortified town as a counterweight to French Louisbourg. Halifax became a key naval base for Britain and later for Canada.
events.html: British settlers arrived to build a fortified town as a counterweight to French Louisbourg. Halifax became a key naval base for Britain and later for Canada.

events.title: New Hampshire's ratification puts the US Constitution into effect
events.description: New Hampshire became the ninth state to ratify, the number required for the Constitution to take effect. The new federal government began work in 1789.
events.html: New Hampshire became the ninth state to ratify, the number required for the Constitution to take effect. The new federal government began work in 1789.

events.title: Louis XVI and his family attempt to flee Paris
events.description: In the night of 20–21 June, King Louis XVI and the royal family tried to leave Paris for Montmédy, where he hoped to regain his freedom. Recognised at Sainte-Menehould, they were stopped and arrested at Varennes-en-Argonne.

events.title: Wellington routs Joseph Bonaparte at Vitoria
events.description: Wellington's Anglo-Portuguese and Spanish army broke the French in northern Spain, capturing their baggage train. Joseph fled, and French rule in Spain collapsed.

events.title: Three civil rights workers are murdered in Mississippi
events.description: James Chaney, Andrew Goodman and Michael Schwerner were killed by Klansmen, with the involvement of local law officers, during Freedom Summer. Their deaths spurred support for the Voting Rights Act of 1965.
